quotes.text: Bon Jovi understood the business of music, and you can hear that in this interview. He knew that to get songs like 'Runaway' played, it was about MTV, but it was about every single market—he had shaken hands with everyone in radio because he wanted to break through.
The bands that were good at performing, and Bon Jovi was one of those bands, got to become an eternal band because they took care of their business.
I feel Jon was trying to write an album using the same old tired formulas as before and even trying to get political. Thinking too much maybe. Bon Jovi is not a political band…in my opinion.

And sadly, at the helm is still John Shanks who has turned the band in to a predictable, paint-by-numbers band that has lost all creativity and imagination. There is no painting outside the lines on this album.

They have turned into a band that tries to be positive and encouraging in their lyrics in a world that is much darker. It feels forced and is presented in a way that might seem bright and fun, but it is boring and a wonderful cure for insomnia.

It is still a lot of emptiness, a lot of boring and a lot of nothing. I think the band needs to shake things up and get rid of Shanks as he isn't pushing them to find anything new or fresh. This is a retread of past albums with less heart and soul.
Jon still trying to be Bruce but he isn't as good a writer and so it comes across as hollow.
I miss a Bon Jovi that tried to shake things up and do something a little different. Stop chasing hits and just write songs that actually mean something to you.

They became tired and boring. They started to lose me here. They became tired and boring. Yeah, there are some good moments, but they were heading down a path of chasing the hit and trying to be something they were not. And that loses authenticity and my respect.
This is the first Bon Jovi album that doesn't keep me fixated from beginning to end.
The production is a little weak as Tico's drums are so lifeless throughout the album. Did they drug him? He is a pounder and yet none of that here.
I feel the story telling was better than it has been and I love the nostalgic feel of some of the songs.

The new album also sees a slightly different band... This time around, it looks like long-time producer (who I wish would stop producing) has wormed his way in to the band full time, a Mr. John Shanks. Lastly, we get Everett Bradley who is there to help with the background vocals and on percussion. I think that is great as the band is trying to help Jon as much as they can vocally.

The opening track, which is also the first single, is "Legendary". A song that pays tribute to this wife but is also a little nostalgic looking at the band's past and looking in to the future as well. It is a song Jon has done a lot lately for opening tracks.

"We Made It Look Easy" is as nostalgic as the opening track maybe even more so. It is Jon taking a look back at his youth and all the things he's done... Jon is sounding good so far and I am really happy for him. Not a heavy rocker at all, but a great soft rock song that makes you feel good looking back.

Next up is "Living Proof" and it brings back the talk box which I don't think we've seen in over decade. As cool as it is to have the talk box back, I will note that it doesn't sound as cool as when Richie does it.
On '2020', Jon really didn't sing so much as speak sing the songs. This time, Jon is singing and I couldn't be happier he seems to be doing better.

"Waves" sees Jon working with more outside writers and this time it is the greta Jason Isbell and I can hear his influence on the song for sure. It is slower tune while the chorus is louder and more upbeat. An AOR track for sure, but again more interesting lyrics and I am really digging what they are putting out here.

Tico's drums on this are driving the beat, but his drums on this album so far have been very muted and that is massive disappointment as he is a pounder. Production wise that sucks (Shanks, I'm talking to you).
One thing I've noticed lately, is Bon Jovi's ballads aren't very good anymore. The song will make you cry, but not for the right reasons.

"The People's House" saves they day. With a "Keep the Faith" bass line (best on the album), we get a charged up, energy filled track. Well, as much energy as they muster nowadays. It is solely written by Jon and it is nice to see he can still do a good song without the help of other peop
